block.comment: Purpose: Paint an RGB gradient one pixel at a time while charts and bars show the colours. No external hardware or AVR image buffer is needed. Wiring: Only the Pro Mini and USB–Serial adapter; the image is generated mathematically. Try: Change the RGB formulas or image dimensions, upload, and watch the computer build the new picture.
Upload, open Plotter at 115200 baud, Connect, then Start. The sketch sends its own dashboard and instructions; no manual configuration is needed.
Fixed incoming line buffer, including room for a terminator. Charts, images and the JSON header stay on the computer/Flash, not in this array.

block.field: @msg Command too long; shorten it and try again.

block.comment: Read one complete newline-terminated command. Partial lines stay in a fixed byte buffer. CR is ignored; oversized commands are discarded. There is no String allocation or waiting for bytes. Expand this reusable function to see the ordinary array and logic blocks.

block.comment: This is an ordinary Serial text message stored in Flash. Click it to edit formatted JSON. The computer creates instruments and computes derived fields; this sketch sends only input values.

block.field: @msg No external hardware. Paint a 32×24 RGB gradient and redraw it with a changing blue channel. Pixel values remain on the computer until overwritten; Save image exports the visible frame. Charts and bars receive the same colour values. Only coordinates and three colours occupy MCU RAM. Press Start to begin; Stop pauses readings.

block.comment: Send this one header from setup and again after Start. It describes the views and gives the next action. Edit this text block to change the dashboard; data order must match fields.
Announce the dashboard immediately after upload/reset, before waiting for Start. Start repeats it if the computer connected later.
Use elapsed milliseconds instead of delay. The command reader remains responsive between updates; unsigned subtraction also works when millis wraps.

No external hardware. Paint a 32×24 RGB gradient and redraw it with a changing blue channel. Pixel values remain on the computer until overwritten; Save image exports the visible frame. Charts and bars receive the same colour values. Only coordinates and three colours occupy MCU RAM. Readings begin on Start. No long delay is used; Stop remains responsive.
